The following minimal working example causes an "invalid universe level, 0 is not greater than 0" error in v4.32.0

abbrev Result (p : Prop) : Type := Option Unit

-- error : "invalid universe level, 0 is not greater than 0"
def test1 {p} : Result p := do
  return ()

-- works fine
set_option backward.do.legacy true in
def test2 {p} : Result p := do
  return ()

-- works fine
def test3 : Option Unit := do
  return ()

When p has type Type instead of Prop, then the universe error disappears, and instead for both test1 and test2 there is an error "failed to synthesize instance of type class Pure Result". When p has type Unit or True then both test1 and test2 work fine.

I am not sure why the behaviour differs depending on the type of p, and I think in all test1 and test2 should work.

Well, it treats the result type syntactically and comes up with monad Result : Prop → Type and result type p; which doesn't work since monads have to have type Type u → Type v. I guess you'd propose that it should unfold Result here? Then the question becomes: in which situations should it unfold Result? Should it just always try for abbrevs?

I think it would make sense to unfold abbrev here, given that abbrev is already unfolded if one would drop the argument p everywhere (i.e. abbrev Result : Type := Option Unit). I am not entirely sure though whether it would make sense to unfold the abbrev when the type of p is Type (or more generally Type u), given that (at least according to the type signature) Result could be a monad in that case. But even then I think it might make sense to unfold abbrev until an instance of Monad(and Pure?) has been found.

do notation wants to look for a instance of Monad Result, which is both not well-typed (Monad requires a Type u -> Type v parameter) and a partial application of Result (thus Result cannot be unfolded to its fully applied definition).

I understand that that is how it works now, but I think that (given that Result is not a monad) the do notation should unfold the abbrev to check whether Result p reduces to a monadic application (as it seems to do in the previous version of the do notation). Or is there a reason why this is not wanted?

Based on the examples I tested, before the do notation seems to unfold the abbrevs until it finds a application m a where m has type Type u → Type v. The example would work when p has type Prop, but not when it has type Type. I did not check the code of the do notation, so maybe someone should confirm what actually happens.
